title: How India's state fuel retailers lose money on every litre of diesel sold

outro.text: Either the pump price rises or taxpayers pay. And that is why

sources: Elara Capital via Financial Express, Oct. 27, 2026
Economic Times / Hindu BusinessLine on Reliance Q2 FY27, Oct. 30, 2026

scenes.hook_card: Diesel costs Rs 95 a litre. Indian retailers still lose Rs 24 on each.
stat: Loss per litre of diesel, Jul-Sep
scenes.text: Diesel in Delhi costs 95 rupees 20 paise a litre. State fuel retailers still lose about 24 rupees on each one.
A year ago they earned 5 rupees a litre. The rupee changed that.

chart.title: Crude cost inside one litre
chart.subtitle: Rupees per litre, Rotation calculation
chart.source: Rotation calculation from Financial Express: Rs 6,310 and Rs 11,732 a barrel

scenes.text: Oil costs the same in dollars as in 2012, but a dollar now buys 95 rupees, not 51. Crude alone costs 74 rupees a litre.

card.title: Diesel, retailer margin per litre
card.source: Elara Capital via Financial Express, Oct. 27, 2026

scenes.text: Elara Capital's estimate: plus 5 rupees last year, minus 24 now.

stat: ICRA: possible FY27 fuel losses, no hike
scenes.text: No hike since May. ICRA says losses could pass 64,000 crore rupees this year.
Reliance sold at world prices and its profit jumped 68 percent. The pump sold at May's price.
